name: Headings of the commentaries (tanbīh, fāʾida, tatimma)
definition: The small headings under which a commentary adds what is not in its text: a warning (tanbīh), a useful point (fāʾida), a completion (tatimma), a closing section (khātima).
body: A tanbīh draws attention to a point the reader might miss or get wrong; a fāʾida adds something useful beside the question; a tatimma or takmila completes a chapter with what the text left out; a khātima closes a book or a part. Al-Suyūṭī's books and the Azhar glosses use them freely, and in Sharḥ Ibn ʿAqīl a 'tanbīh' often settles a point of the Alfiyya's wording.
